finding: The live range of $160-$675 is a little low at both ends. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2013 Civic 1.8L about $222-$600 (0.5-2.0 hr); midsize 2020 Hyundai Sonata 2.5L about $409-$555 (2.4 hr); truck 2003 F-150 5.4L about $200-$473 (1.0-2.0 hr); luxury 2012 Lexus CT 200h about $514-$737 (1.9 hr). Across the four the span is about $200-$737. The lowest total we can build is about $200, and that uses an $80 store-brand valve and one hour; $160 is below anything found. The $675 top holds for engines with the valve on top, but not where the valve is buried or costly: the Lexus CT 200h (and the Toyota Prius, which shares its valve and its 1.9 hr maker time) builds to about $737, a 2018-2023 F-150 valve lists at $416 and a 2025 Ram 1500 3.6L valve at $412 (about $730-$740 with two hours), the Civic Hybrid valve lists at $735 before labor, and YourMechanic shows $835 for a 2012 BMW 328i. Diesel EGR valves and EGR coolers are a different, larger job and are not covered by this range. What changed on the second look (2026-11-20): the midsize example moved from the Honda Odyssey to the 2020 Hyundai Sonata 2.5L and the luxury example from the Acura TL to the 2012 Lexus CT 200h, because each has a maker time for the valve on that vehicle. The Odyssey's 0.4 hr was dropped as a range end because Honda's operation also includes a software update, and the TL had only that borrowed figure. How solid the labor times are: two are maker warranty times for the example vehicle itself. Hyundai's 2.4 hr for 'Replace EGR Valve' on the 2020 Sonata 2.5L is the cleanest and is repeated in a 2024 campaign. Lexus's 1.9 hr for 'R & R Exhaust Recirculation Valve' on the CT 200h comes from a bulletin whose procedure also re-tapes a harness tie and clears codes, so the valve alone may be slightly less. Both are single warranty figures, so those two classes have no spread and a shop will often bill more. The Civic has no maker time: its low end (0.5 hr) is a general how-to guide's '30 to 60 minutes' and its high end a general 'one to two hours'; maker times for other small cars bracket it (Kia Niro hybrid 0.6 hr, Toyota Prius 1.9 hr) but are not the Civic. The truck low end is a parts seller's 'approx 1 hour' for the F-150 and its high end the same general statement; no maker time was found for a gasoline half-ton truck. Maker times show how much the job varies with where the valve sits: 0.4-0.6 hr on a Honda V6, Kia Niro hybrid or Hyundai Sonata Hybrid, 1.6 hr on a Kia Carnival, 1.9 hr on a Prius, 2.4-2.6 hr on a Hyundai Sonata, Tucson or Kia Sportage 2.5L. On parts: no aftermarket valve was found for the Sonata 2.5L, so its low end is the genuine valve at a discount, and the Sonata job also needs several EGR and exhaust gaskets that are not priced here. The truck example is an older F-150 because most newer gasoline half-ton trucks have no separate EGR valve; where they do, the part costs two to three times as much. Our totals sit below RepairPal ($489-$632) at the low end mainly on parts: its parts figure is $308-$367, while list prices we can cite run from $153 to $434.
extras: A quote often adds a diagnosis fee (an EGR code can also be caused by clogged passages, a sensor, wiring or a vacuum fault, so the valve is not always the cure), cleaning of carbon-clogged EGR passages or the intake, a new gasket if not supplied with the valve, shop supplies and sales tax. Some vehicles need a software update or an idle or EGR relearn after the swap. An EGR tube or pipe is sometimes replaced at the same time. The EGR cooler, fitted to diesels and some newer gasoline engines, is a separate and much larger job: for example a 2025 Ram 1500 3.6L cooler lists at $857 against $412 for the valve.
